CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE
OF THE
MARRICKVILLE MUNICIPAL LIBRARY COMMITTEE

Adopted by resolution of the Marrickville Municipal Council at its meeting held on the third day of April, 1962.

---

PREAMBLE

WHEREAS the Council of the Municipality of Marrickville deems it expedient to establish a standing committee to advise the Council upon the provision, maintenance, and development of municipal library services for the inhabitants of the Municipality;

AND WHEREAS it is desirable that the said committee shall comprise persons having knowledge of or interest in library affairs, together with representatives of the Council, so that the library service may be conducted in accordance with the best standards of public librarianship and with due regard to the needs of the community;

AND WHEREAS it is intended that the committee shall act in an advisory capacity only, and that all final decisions respecting the expenditure of moneys, the appointment of staff, and the adoption of policies shall remain with the Council;

NOW THEREFORE the Council hereby establishes the Marrickville Municipal Library Committee, to be known also as "the Committee," and prescribes the following Charter and Terms of Reference.

---

PART I — ESTABLISHMENT AND PURPOSE

1. The Marrickville Municipal Library Committee established_date 1962-04-03 date. Record status: current. The Committee is hereby constituted as a standing advisory committee of the Marrickville Municipal Council, and shall be known as the Marrickville Municipal Library Committee.

2. The objects of the Committee shall be:

(a) to advise the Council upon all matters relating to the establishment, extension, and improvement of the municipal library service;

(b) to promote the use of the library by all sections of the community, including children, young persons, adults, and persons with special needs;

(c) to assist in the formation of a library collection which shall be of educational, cultural, informational, and recreational value to the inhabitants of the Municipality;

(d) to encourage co-operation between the library and other educational, cultural, and welfare organisations within the Municipality; and

(e) to report to the Council from time to time upon the state of the library service and upon any matters referred to the Committee by the Council.

3. The Committee shall not have power to expend moneys, to enter into contracts, or to engage or dismiss staff, save as expressly authorised by the Council in writing.

---

PART II — MEMBERSHIP

4. The Committee shall consist of not fewer than seven and not more than eleven members, appointed by the Council, as follows:

(a) three members of the Council, to be nominated by the Council;

(b) not fewer than two and not more than four persons ordinarily resident within the Municipality, being persons who, in the opinion of the Council, have knowledge of or interest in library affairs;

(c) one person nominated by the trustees of any library established under the Library Act 1939, if such trustees exist within the Municipality; and

(d) such other persons, not exceeding two, as the Council may from time to time appoint by reason of their special knowledge or experience.

5. Members shall be appointed for a term of two years, save that members of the Council shall hold office during their term as councillors. A member appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the member whom he or she replaces.

6. The Council shall appoint one of the members to be Chairperson of the Committee, and one to be Deputy Chairperson. The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which he or she is present.
**14.** The Committee is established pursuant to the powers conferred upon the Council by the Library Act 1939 (as amended) and the Local Government Act 1919 (as amended). The Committee acts as the library committee of the Council, and its functions are advisory and recommendatory in nature except where the Council has delegated specific functions in writing.

**15.** The Committee shall furnish to the Council an annual report upon the work of the Committee and the state of the library service, including a statement of receipts and expenditure, and shall make such other reports as the Council may require.

**16.** The Committee shall not incur any expenditure, whether by way of purchase, maintenance, or otherwise, without the prior approval of the Council, save for expenditure from petty cash funds advanced by the Council for the purpose, which shall be accounted for at each meeting.

**17.** All property acquired by the Committee shall be vested in the Council, and shall be held by the Council on trust for the purposes of the library service.

---

**PART V — AMENDMENTS**

**18.** This Charter may be amended by resolution of the Council, but no amendment shall be effective unless it has been proposed at a meeting of the Committee and referred to the Council with the Committee's recommendation, or unless the amendment is proposed by the Council itself. The Committee shall be notified of any amendment proposed by the Council and shall have the opportunity to make representations to the Council before the amendment is adopted.

**19.** A copy of this Charter, as amended from time to time, shall be kept at the library and shall be available for inspection by members of the public during ordinary business hours.

---

**HISTORICAL NOTE**

This Charter, and the Committee established by it, operated in respect of the Municipality of Marrickville until the municipal council ceased to exist as a separate local government area. Under the NSW Local Government Act, Marrickville Council merged into Inner West Council. Record status: historical. The Committee's functions and the provisions of this Charter were assumed by the Inner West Council, which continued to administer the library service formerly provided by the Municipality of Marrickville. The Inner West Council resolved at its first ordinary meeting to adopt the existing arrangements for the library service on an interim basis, pending the preparation of new terms of reference for a library committee of the Inner West Council. This historical note is included for the assistance of readers of the archive copy of this Charter; it forms no part of the terms of reference as they applied to the Committee.

---

**PART VI — TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS (as amended 11 November 2008)**

**20.** Wherever in this Charter the expression "the Municipality" or "the Council" appears, it shall be read and construed as referring to the local government authority for the time being responsible for the administration of the library service to which this Charter relates.

**21.** Any reference to the Library Act 1939 shall be read as including any Act amending or replacing that Act, and any reference to the Local Government Act 1919 shall be read as including the Local Government Act 1993.

---

**SIGNED** on behalf of the Council of the Municipality of Marrickville on 11 November 2008.

*(Signature)*

**N. O'BRIEN**
Town Clerk

---

*This copy of the Charter has been reproduced from the records of the Marrickville Municipal Library Committee archive, held by Inner West Council. Where the original document contained marginal annotations, they have been noted in square brackets. Typographical errors in the original have been preserved.*
**PART VII — COMMITTEE OPERATIONS AND MEETING PROCEDURES (as amended 11 November 2008)**

**22.** The Committee shall meet at least four times in each calendar year. Meetings shall be held at such times and places as the Committee may determine, provided that the first meeting of the Committee in each calendar year shall be convened by the Town Clerk not later than the end of February.

**23.** The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**24.** A quorum shall consist of one-third of the members of the Committee for the time being holding office, but in no case shall a quorum be less than three members. No business shall be transacted at any meeting of the Committee unless a quorum is present.

**25.** Each member of the Committee present at a meeting shall have one vote. Subject to clause 26, all questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The person presiding at the meeting shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, shall also have a casting vote.

**26.** No member of the Committee shall vote on any question in which the member has a pecuniary interest, whether direct or indirect, and the member shall not be counted in a quorum for the purposes of that question. A member who has such an interest shall disclose the nature of the interest to the Committee before the question is put.

**27.** The Committee may from time to time appoint sub-committees for the purpose of inquiring into and reporting upon any matter within the scope of the Committee's functions. A sub-committee shall consist of such members of the Committee and such other persons as the Committee may determine. The Committee may delegate to a sub-committee such of its functions as it thinks fit, but no sub-committee shall have power to expend money on behalf of the Committee or the Council without the prior approval of the Committee.

**28.** Minutes shall be kept of the proceedings of each meeting of the Committee and of each sub-committee. The minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Committee or sub-committee, as the case may be, and shall be signed by the person presiding at the meeting at which they are confirmed.

**29.** Notice of each meeting of the Committee shall be given to each member not less than seven days before the date of the meeting. The notice shall specify the business to be transacted at the meeting. A member may, with the consent of the Chairperson, waive the requirement for notice in respect of any particular meeting.

**30.** The Committee shall cause proper records to be kept of its proceedings and of the attendance of members at meetings. The records shall be open for inspection by members of the public at the library during ordinary business hours, subject to the exclusion of any matter that the Committee determines to be confidential.

**31.** The Town Clerk shall act as secretary to the Committee and shall, in that capacity, attend all meetings of the Committee unless excused by the Committee. In the absence of the Town Clerk, the Town Clerk's nominee shall attend and act as secretary.

---

**PART VIII — FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

**32.** The Council shall provide the Committee with such funds as the Council considers necessary for the maintenance and operation of the library service. The Committee shall submit to the Council, not later than 31 March in each year, an estimate of its expenditure for the following financial year.
**PART IX — REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

**33.** The Committee shall, not later than 31 August in each year, submit to the Council a report upon the operation of the library service during the preceding financial year. The report shall include particulars of the number of volumes added to the library during the year, the number of volumes withdrawn, the number of registered borrowers, the total number of books lent, and such other matters as the Committee thinks fit or as the Council may require.

**34.** The report referred to in clause 33 shall be presented to the Council at its first ordinary meeting after the receipt of the report, and the Council shall cause the report to be laid upon the table of the Council chamber for the information of aldermen.

**35.** The Committee shall furnish to the Council, at such times as the Council may require, such information concerning the library service as the Council may from time to time request.

**36.** The Committee shall cause an annual statement of receipts and expenditure to be prepared and submitted to the Council, together with the report referred to in clause 33. The statement shall be in such form as the Council may approve.

---

**PART X — GENERAL PROVISIONS**

**37.** The Committee may, with the approval of the Council, purchase, lease, or otherwise acquire any land, buildings, or equipment necessary for the purposes of the library service. Any such acquisition shall be effected in the name of the Council.

**38.** The Committee may accept gifts, bequests, and donations of books, money, or other property for the purposes of the library service. All such gifts, bequests, and donations shall be acknowledged in writing by the Town Clerk on behalf of the Committee, and shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting of the Committee.

**39.** The Committee shall not incur any expenditure in excess of the funds provided by the Council for the financial year, except with the prior approval of the Council.

**40.** The Committee shall have power to make by-laws and regulations, not inconsistent with this Charter or with any ordinance of the Council, for the good government of the library and for the regulation of the use of the library by the public. All such by-laws and regulations shall be subject to the approval of the Council.

**41.** The Committee shall cause to be prepared, and shall keep under review, a collection development policy for the library. The policy shall address the selection, acquisition, and withdrawal of library materials, and shall have regard to the needs of the diverse communities served by the library.

**42.** The Committee shall have regard to the preservation of the local history collection and shall take such steps as are necessary to ensure the proper storage, cataloguing, and conservation of materials in that collection.

---

**PART XI — AMENDMENT OF CHARTER**

**43.** This Charter may be amended from time to time by resolution of the Council. A proposed amendment may be initiated by the Committee or by the Council.

**44.** Where a proposed amendment is initiated by the Committee, the Committee shall submit the proposed amendment to the Council in writing, together with a statement of the reasons for the proposed amendment.

**45.** Where a proposed amendment is initiated by the Council, the Council shall cause notice of the proposed amendment to be given to the Committee, and the Committee shall have the opportunity to make representations to the Council in respect of the proposed amendment before the Council proceeds to consider it.

**46.** No amendment to this Charter shall have effect until it has been adopted by resolution of the Council and recorded in the minutes of the Council meeting at which it was adopted.
**PART XII — GENERAL PROVISIONS**

**47.** The Committee shall meet at least once in every three calendar months, and at such other times as the Committee may determine. Meetings shall be held at such place and time as the Committee may from time to time appoint.

**48.** The Chairperson, or in the Chairperson's absence the Deputy Chairperson, shall preside at every meeting of the Committee. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**49.** A question arising at a meeting of the Committee shall be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting on that question. Each member present shall have one vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the person presiding shall have a second or casting vote.

**50.** No business shall be transacted at a meeting of the Committee unless a quorum of members is present at the time the business is transacted. Five members shall constitute a quorum.

**51.** The Committee may appoint sub-committees from among its members and may delegate to any such sub-committee such of its functions as it thinks fit, subject to such conditions as it may impose. A sub-committee shall report its proceedings to the Committee at the next meeting of the Committee after the proceedings occur.

**52.** The Committee shall keep minutes of its proceedings. Minutes of each meeting shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Committee, and shall be signed by the person presiding at that next meeting. Upon confirmation, the minutes shall be entered in a book kept for that purpose and shall be open to inspection by any member of the public at the library during ordinary opening hours, subject to the exclusion of any matter which the Committee determines to be confidential.

**53.** The Committee shall report to the Council from time to time, and at least once in each year, upon the operation of the library and upon the exercise and performance of the Committee's functions under this Charter.

**54.** The Committee shall cause proper accounts to be kept of all money received and expended by the Committee, and such accounts shall be audited as the Council may direct.

**55.** The Committee shall, before the end of each financial year, submit to the Council an estimate of the expenditure which the Committee considers will be necessary for the maintenance and operation of the library in the next financial year.

**56.** The Committee shall have the custody of all books, documents, and other property belonging to the library, and shall be responsible for their safe keeping.

**57.** No member of the Committee shall be personally liable for any loss or damage arising out of the exercise or purported exercise of the Committee's functions under this Charter, unless the loss or damage is caused by the member's own wilful act, neglect, or default.

**58.** The Committee may, with the approval of the Council, accept gifts, bequests, and donations for the purposes of the library, whether such gifts, bequests, or donations are subject to conditions or otherwise. Any such conditions shall be reported to the Council.

**59.** The Committee shall have regard to the requirements of the Library Act and any regulations made thereunder, and to any directions given by the Council in relation to the library.

**60.** The Committee shall have power to do all such things as are incidental to, or consequential upon, the exercise and performance of its functions under this Charter.

---

**PART XIII — TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS**

**61.** Upon the coming into operation of this Charter, all property, assets, books, records, and other documents held by or on behalf of the Committee immediately prior to that time shall continue to be held by the Committee.

**Resolution 18/10/16/02:** That the Library Manager be authorised to proceed with the weeding of the adult non-fiction collection as detailed in her report, and that withdrawn items be offered to the Friends of the Library for their book sale, with any remainder to be disposed of in accordance with council policy.
**Marrickville Municipal Library Committee Meeting Minutes**

**Meeting 18/06 – 16 October 2018**

**6. Volunteer Coordination**

6.1 The Library Manager, Ms Moretti, reported that the volunteer program continues to operate
successfully, with 28 active volunteers currently assisting across the library’s branches. This
includes 12 volunteers who support the English conversation classes, 9 who assist with the home
library service, and 7 who help with shelving and general duties.

6.2 Ms Moretti advised that a volunteer information session was held on 2 October, with 6
prospective volunteers attending. Of these, 4 have submitted applications and are currently
undergoing the recruitment process, which includes a working with children check and a reference
check. It is anticipated that the new volunteers will commence their orientation in early November.

6.3 Concerns were raised by Cr Papadopoulos regarding the consistency of volunteer training,
particularly in relation to the home library service. He noted that some volunteers had expressed
uncertainty about the procedure for reporting delivery issues. Ms Moretti acknowledged this and
advised that a refresher session for existing volunteers would be scheduled for late November.
The session will cover the updated delivery log procedure and the new client feedback form.

6.4 The Chair thanked the volunteers for their ongoing contribution and noted that their work is
highly valued by the community. It was suggested that a small end-of-year gathering be held to
acknowledge their efforts. Ms Moretti agreed to coordinate this with the Friends of the Library,
with a provisional date to be confirmed at the next meeting.

**7. Community Group Partnerships**

7.1 Ms Moretti provided an update on the library’s partnerships with local community groups.
The partnership with the Marrickville Community Garden continues, with the garden’s produce
display now located near the library’s main entrance. The display has generated interest among
borrowers, and the garden has reported an increase in enquiries about their activities.

7.2 The committee noted the ongoing collaboration with the Marrickville Historical Society.
The society has been assisting with the digitisation of local history photographs, and a selection
of these images is currently on display in the local history room. The display will remain in
place until the end of November.

7.3 Ms Moretti reported that the library has been approached by the Marrickville Seniors
Centre regarding a potential partnership for a series of intergenerational reading sessions.
The proposal is for school-aged children to read with seniors on a monthly basis. Ms Moretti
advised that she is supportive of the idea in principle, and will prepare a detailed proposal for
the committee’s consideration at the next meeting.

7.4 The committee discussed the importance of maintaining strong relationships with local
community groups, and agreed that the library’s role as a community hub is a key priority.
It was noted that the library’s meeting rooms are well utilised by community groups, with an
average of 15 bookings per month.

**8. Financial Report**

8.1 The Library Manager tabled the financial report for the period 1 September to 30 September
2018. The report was noted as being consistent with the budget, with no significant variances
identified.

8.2 *Expenditure* – Total expenditure for September was $182,400, which is 8.2% of the annual
budget. The main areas of expenditure were staff salaries ($121,000), collection development
($28,500), and programs and events ($12,900). The expenditure on collection development was
slightly higher than anticipated due to the purchase of new non-fiction titles, which was
approved at the previous meeting.
**10. Other Business**

10.1 The committee noted that the Library will be closed on the second Monday of
November for staff professional development. The closure is consistent with the
arrangement approved by Council, and notices have been placed on the Library
website and at the front desk. The Library will reopen at 9.30am the following day.

10.2 Councillor Nguyen raised the matter of the library’s volunteer program. He
asked whether the committee had received an update on the number of active
volunteers, as the figure had not been reported for some time. The Library
Manager advised that a full volunteer report has been scheduled for the February
2019 meeting, and that current volunteer numbers are stable. She confirmed that
the volunteer coordinator position remains vacant, and that recruitment for that
role is being handled by Council’s HR section. Councillor Nguyen asked that the
report include a breakdown of volunteer hours by activity, and the Library
Manager agreed to include this.

10.3 Cr Demetriou asked whether the library had given any further thought to
extending the opening hours on Wednesday evenings. The Library Manager advised
that the matter had been discussed with Council’s property section, and that a
costing had been prepared. The costing assumes an additional two hours per week,
with staffing provided by a combination of existing casual staff and a new
permanent part-time position. The Library Manager will circulate the costing to
committee members by email prior to the next meeting, and the matter will be
listed for discussion under other business at that time.

10.4 The committee discussed the proposal from the Marrickville Seniors Centre
regarding intergenerational reading sessions, which was raised earlier in the
meeting. It was agreed that Ms Moretti would bring a draft proposal to the next
meeting, and that the proposal should include an outline of the session format,
an indication of the number of children and seniors that could be accommodated,
and a plan for the recruitment of child participants through local primary
schools. The committee expressed general support for the concept, and noted that
the Library’s meeting room would be a suitable venue.

**11. Reports from Sub-Committees and Working Groups**

11.1 The Library Manager reported that the Local History Working Group had met
on 2 October 2018. The group has been focused on the digitisation of the
Marrickville area’s early council rate books, which are held in the local
history collection. The group has completed the scanning of the rate books for
the years 1890 to 1895, and is now in the process of checking the quality of the
scans and preparing the associated index. The index is being prepared by
volunteers, and the group expects the work to be completed by the end of the
year. A short article on the project will be included in the next edition of the
library’s newsletter.

11.2 The Library Manager reported that the Children’s and Youth Services Working
Group had met on 9 October 2018. The group discussed the summer school holiday
program, which is currently being planned. The program will run from mid-
December 2018 to the end of January 2019, and will include a mix of free and
low-cost activities. The group has confirmed that the popular “Lego Club” will
be offered on a weekly basis, and that a new robotics workshop will be
introduced, subject to the availability of a suitable facilitator. The Library
Manager will provide a more detailed program outline at the next meeting.

11.3 The committee noted the minutes of the two working groups, which had been
circulated with the agenda.

**12. Staff Matters**

12.1 The Library Manager reported that the temporary library assistant who had
been employed to cover maternity leave has had her contract extended for a
further three months. The extension is effective from 1 November 2018, and will
ensure continuity of staffing through the busy summer period.

CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE
OF THE
MARRICKVILLE MUNICIPAL LIBRARY COMMITTEE

Adopted by resolution of the Marrickville Municipal Council at its meeting held on the third day of April, 1962.

---

PREAMBLE

WHEREAS the Council of the Municipality of Marrickville deems it expedient to establish a standing committee to advise the Council upon the provision, maintenance, and development of municipal library services for the inhabitants of the Municipality;

AND WHEREAS it is desirable that the said committee shall comprise persons having knowledge of or interest in library affairs, together with representatives of the Council, so that the library service may be conducted in accordance with the best standards of public librarianship and with due regard to the needs of the community;

AND WHEREAS it is intended that the committee shall act in an advisory capacity only, and that all final decisions respecting the expenditure of moneys, the appointment of staff, and the adoption of policies shall remain with the Council;

NOW THEREFORE the Council hereby establishes the Marrickville Municipal Library Committee, to be known also as "the Committee," and prescribes the following Charter and Terms of Reference.

---

PART I — ESTABLISHMENT AND PURPOSE

1. The Marrickville Municipal Library Committee established_date 1962-04-03 date. Record status: current. The Committee is hereby constituted as a standing advisory committee of the Marrickville Municipal Council, and shall be known as the Marrickville Municipal Library Committee.

2. The objects of the Committee shall be:

(a) to advise the Council upon all matters relating to the establishment, extension, and improvement of the municipal library service;

(b) to promote the use of the library by all sections of the community, including children, young persons, adults, and persons with special needs;

(c) to assist in the formation of a library collection which shall be of educational, cultural, informational, and recreational value to the inhabitants of the Municipality;

(d) to encourage co-operation between the library and other educational, cultural, and welfare organisations within the Municipality; and

(e) to report to the Council from time to time upon the state of the library service and upon any matters referred to the Committee by the Council.

3. The Committee shall not have power to expend moneys, to enter into contracts, or to engage or dismiss staff, save as expressly authorised by the Council in writing.

---

PART II — MEMBERSHIP

4. The Committee shall consist of not fewer than seven and not more than eleven members, appointed by the Council, as follows:

(a) three members of the Council, to be nominated by the Council;

(b) not fewer than two and not more than four persons ordinarily resident within the Municipality, being persons who, in the opinion of the Council, have knowledge of or interest in library affairs;

(c) one person nominated by the trustees of any library established under the Library Act 1939, if such trustees exist within the Municipality; and

(d) such other persons, not exceeding two, as the Council may from time to time appoint by reason of their special knowledge or experience.

5. Members shall be appointed for a term of two years, save that members of the Council shall hold office during their term as councillors. A member appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the member whom he or she replaces.

6. The Council shall appoint one of the members to be Chairperson of the Committee, and one to be Deputy Chairperson. The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which he or she is present.

**14.** The Committee is established pursuant to the powers conferred upon the Council by the Library Act 1939 (as amended) and the Local Government Act 1919 (as amended). The Committee acts as the library committee of the Council, and its functions are advisory and recommendatory in nature except where the Council has delegated specific functions in writing.

**15.** The Committee shall furnish to the Council an annual report upon the work of the Committee and the state of the library service, including a statement of receipts and expenditure, and shall make such other reports as the Council may require.

**16.** The Committee shall not incur any expenditure, whether by way of purchase, maintenance, or otherwise, without the prior approval of the Council, save for expenditure from petty cash funds advanced by the Council for the purpose, which shall be accounted for at each meeting.

**17.** All property acquired by the Committee shall be vested in the Council, and shall be held by the Council on trust for the purposes of the library service.

---

**PART V — AMENDMENTS**

**18.** This Charter may be amended by resolution of the Council, but no amendment shall be effective unless it has been proposed at a meeting of the Committee and referred to the Council with the Committee's recommendation, or unless the amendment is proposed by the Council itself. The Committee shall be notified of any amendment proposed by the Council and shall have the opportunity to make representations to the Council before the amendment is adopted.

**19.** A copy of this Charter, as amended from time to time, shall be kept at the library and shall be available for inspection by members of the public during ordinary business hours.

---

**HISTORICAL NOTE**

This Charter, and the Committee established by it, operated in respect of the Municipality of Marrickville until the municipal council ceased to exist as a separate local government area. Under the NSW Local Government Act, Marrickville Council merged into Inner West Council. Record status: historical. The Committee's functions and the provisions of this Charter were assumed by the Inner West Council, which continued to administer the library service formerly provided by the Municipality of Marrickville. The Inner West Council resolved at its first ordinary meeting to adopt the existing arrangements for the library service on an interim basis, pending the preparation of new terms of reference for a library committee of the Inner West Council. This historical note is included for the assistance of readers of the archive copy of this Charter; it forms no part of the terms of reference as they applied to the Committee.

---

**PART VI — TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS (as amended 11 November 2008)**

**20.** Wherever in this Charter the expression "the Municipality" or "the Council" appears, it shall be read and construed as referring to the local government authority for the time being responsible for the administration of the library service to which this Charter relates.

**21.** Any reference to the Library Act 1939 shall be read as including any Act amending or replacing that Act, and any reference to the Local Government Act 1919 shall be read as including the Local Government Act 1993.

---

**SIGNED** on behalf of the Council of the Municipality of Marrickville on 11 November 2008.

*(Signature)*

**N. O'BRIEN**
Town Clerk

---

Where the original document contained marginal annotations, they have been noted in square brackets. Typographical errors in the original have been preserved.*

**PART VII — COMMITTEE OPERATIONS AND MEETING PROCEDURES (as amended 11 November 2008)**

**22.** The Committee shall meet at least four times in each calendar year. Meetings shall be held at such times and places as the Committee may determine, provided that the first meeting of the Committee in each calendar year shall be convened by the Town Clerk not later than the end of February.

**23.** The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**24.** A quorum shall consist of one-third of the members of the Committee for the time being holding office, but in no case shall a quorum be less than three members. No business shall be transacted at any meeting of the Committee unless a quorum is present.

**25.** Each member of the Committee present at a meeting shall have one vote. Subject to clause 26, all questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The person presiding at the meeting shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, shall also have a casting vote.

**26.** No member of the Committee shall vote on any question in which the member has a pecuniary interest, whether direct or indirect, and the member shall not be counted in a quorum for the purposes of that question. A member who has such an interest shall disclose the nature of the interest to the Committee before the question is put.

**27.** The Committee may from time to time appoint sub-committees for the purpose of inquiring into and reporting upon any matter within the scope of the Committee's functions. A sub-committee shall consist of such members of the Committee and such other persons as the Committee may determine. The Committee may delegate to a sub-committee such of its functions as it thinks fit, but no sub-committee shall have power to expend money on behalf of the Committee or the Council without the prior approval of the Committee.

**28.** Minutes shall be kept of the proceedings of each meeting of the Committee and of each sub-committee. The minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Committee or sub-committee, as the case may be, and shall be signed by the person presiding at the meeting at which they are confirmed.

**29.** Notice of each meeting of the Committee shall be given to each member not less than seven days before the date of the meeting. The notice shall specify the business to be transacted at the meeting. A member may, with the consent of the Chairperson, waive the requirement for notice in respect of any particular meeting.

**30.** The Committee shall cause proper records to be kept of its proceedings and of the attendance of members at meetings. The records shall be open for inspection by members of the public at the library during ordinary business hours, subject to the exclusion of any matter that the Committee determines to be confidential.

**31.** The Town Clerk shall act as secretary to the Committee and shall, in that capacity, attend all meetings of the Committee unless excused by the Committee. In the absence of the Town Clerk, the Town Clerk's nominee shall attend and act as secretary.

---

**PART VIII — FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

**32.** The Council shall provide the Committee with such funds as the Council considers necessary for the maintenance and operation of the library service. The Committee shall submit to the Council, not later than 31 March in each year, an estimate of its expenditure for the following financial year.

**PART IX — REPORTING AND ACCOUNTABILITY**

**33.** The Committee shall, not later than 31 August in each year, submit to the Council a report upon the operation of the library service during the preceding financial year. The report shall include particulars of the number of volumes added to the library during the year, the number of volumes withdrawn, the number of registered borrowers, the total number of books lent, and such other matters as the Committee thinks fit or as the Council may require.

**34.** The report referred to in clause 33 shall be presented to the Council at its first ordinary meeting after the receipt of the report, and the Council shall cause the report to be laid upon the table of the Council chamber for the information of aldermen.

**35.** The Committee shall furnish to the Council, at such times as the Council may require, such information concerning the library service as the Council may from time to time request.

**36.** The Committee shall cause an annual statement of receipts and expenditure to be prepared and submitted to the Council, together with the report referred to in clause 33. The statement shall be in such form as the Council may approve.

---

**PART X — GENERAL PROVISIONS**

**37.** The Committee may, with the approval of the Council, purchase, lease, or otherwise acquire any land, buildings, or equipment necessary for the purposes of the library service. Any such acquisition shall be effected in the name of the Council.

**38.** The Committee may accept gifts, bequests, and donations of books, money, or other property for the purposes of the library service. All such gifts, bequests, and donations shall be acknowledged in writing by the Town Clerk on behalf of the Committee, and shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting of the Committee.

**39.** The Committee shall not incur any expenditure in excess of the funds provided by the Council for the financial year, except with the prior approval of the Council.

**40.** The Committee shall have power to make by-laws and regulations, not inconsistent with this Charter or with any ordinance of the Council, for the good government of the library and for the regulation of the use of the library by the public. All such by-laws and regulations shall be subject to the approval of the Council.

**41.** The Committee shall cause to be prepared, and shall keep under review, a collection development policy for the library. The policy shall address the selection, acquisition, and withdrawal of library materials, and shall have regard to the needs of the diverse communities served by the library.

**42.** The Committee shall have regard to the preservation of the local history collection and shall take such steps as are necessary to ensure the proper storage, cataloguing, and conservation of materials in that collection.

---

**PART XI — AMENDMENT OF CHARTER**

**43.** This Charter may be amended from time to time by resolution of the Council. A proposed amendment may be initiated by the Committee or by the Council.

**44.** Where a proposed amendment is initiated by the Committee, the Committee shall submit the proposed amendment to the Council in writing, together with a statement of the reasons for the proposed amendment.

**45.** Where a proposed amendment is initiated by the Council, the Council shall cause notice of the proposed amendment to be given to the Committee, and the Committee shall have the opportunity to make representations to the Council in respect of the proposed amendment before the Council proceeds to consider it.

**46.** No amendment to this Charter shall have effect until it has been adopted by resolution of the Council and recorded in the minutes of the Council meeting at which it was adopted.

**PART XII — GENERAL PROVISIONS**

**47.** The Committee shall meet at least once in every three calendar months, and at such other times as the Committee may determine. Meetings shall be held at such place and time as the Committee may from time to time appoint.

**48.** The Chairperson, or in the Chairperson's absence the Deputy Chairperson, shall preside at every meeting of the Committee. In the absence of both the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

**49.** A question arising at a meeting of the Committee shall be decided by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting on that question. Each member present shall have one vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the person presiding shall have a second or casting vote.

**50.** No business shall be transacted at a meeting of the Committee unless a quorum of members is present at the time the business is transacted. Five members shall constitute a quorum.

**51.** The Committee may appoint sub-committees from among its members and may delegate to any such sub-committee such of its functions as it thinks fit, subject to such conditions as it may impose. A sub-committee shall report its proceedings to the Committee at the next meeting of the Committee after the proceedings occur.

**52.** The Committee shall keep minutes of its proceedings. Minutes of each meeting shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Committee, and shall be signed by the person presiding at that next meeting. Upon confirmation, the minutes shall be entered in a book kept for that purpose and shall be open to inspection by any member of the public at the library during ordinary opening hours, subject to the exclusion of any matter which the Committee determines to be confidential.

**53.** The Committee shall report to the Council from time to time, and at least once in each year, upon the operation of the library and upon the exercise and performance of the Committee's functions under this Charter.

**54.** The Committee shall cause proper accounts to be kept of all money received and expended by the Committee, and such accounts shall be audited as the Council may direct.

**55.** The Committee shall, before the end of each financial year, submit to the Council an estimate of the expenditure which the Committee considers will be necessary for the maintenance and operation of the library in the next financial year.

**56.** The Committee shall have the custody of all books, documents, and other property belonging to the library, and shall be responsible for their safe keeping.

**57.** No member of the Committee shall be personally liable for any loss or damage arising out of the exercise or purported exercise of the Committee's functions under this Charter, unless the loss or damage is caused by the member's own wilful act, neglect, or default.

**58.** The Committee may, with the approval of the Council, accept gifts, bequests, and donations for the purposes of the library, whether such gifts, bequests, or donations are subject to conditions or otherwise. Any such conditions shall be reported to the Council.

**59.** The Committee shall have regard to the requirements of the Library Act and any regulations made thereunder, and to any directions given by the Council in relation to the library.

**60.** The Committee shall have power to do all such things as are incidental to, or consequential upon, the exercise and performance of its functions under this Charter.

---

**PART XIII — TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS**

**61.** Upon the coming into operation of this Charter, all property, assets, books, records, and other documents held by or on behalf of the Committee immediately prior to that time shall continue to be held by the Committee.

**Marrickville Municipal Library Committee Meeting Minutes**

**Meeting 18/06 – 16 October 2018**

**6. Volunteer Coordination**

6.1 The Library Manager, Ms Moretti, reported that the volunteer program continues to operate
successfully, with 28 active volunteers currently assisting across the library’s branches. This
includes 12 volunteers who support the English conversation classes, 9 who assist with the home
library service, and 7 who help with shelving and general duties.

6.2 Ms Moretti advised that a volunteer information session was held on 2 October, with 6
prospective volunteers attending. Of these, 4 have submitted applications and are currently
undergoing the recruitment process, which includes a working with children check and a reference
check. It is anticipated that the new volunteers will commence their orientation in early November.

6.3 Concerns were raised by Cr Papadopoulos regarding the consistency of volunteer training,
particularly in relation to the home library service. He noted that some volunteers had expressed
uncertainty about the procedure for reporting delivery issues. Ms Moretti acknowledged this and
advised that a refresher session for existing volunteers would be scheduled for late November.
The session will cover the updated delivery log procedure and the new client feedback form.

6.4 The Chair thanked the volunteers for their ongoing contribution and noted that their work is
highly valued by the community. It was suggested that a small end-of-year gathering be held to
acknowledge their efforts. Ms Moretti agreed to coordinate this with the Friends of the Library,
with a provisional date to be confirmed at the next meeting.

**7. Community Group Partnerships**

7.1 Ms Moretti provided an update on the library’s partnerships with local community groups.
The partnership with the Marrickville Community Garden continues, with the garden’s produce
display now located near the library’s main entrance. The display has generated interest among
borrowers, and the garden has reported an increase in enquiries about their activities.

7.2 The committee noted the ongoing collaboration with the Marrickville Historical Society.
The society has been assisting with the digitisation of local history photographs, and a selection
of these images is currently on display in the local history room. The display will remain in
place until the end of November.

7.3 Ms Moretti reported that the library has been approached by the Marrickville Seniors
Centre regarding a potential partnership for a series of intergenerational reading sessions.
The proposal is for school-aged children to read with seniors on a monthly basis. Ms Moretti
advised that she is supportive of the idea in principle, and will prepare a detailed proposal for
the committee’s consideration at the next meeting.

7.4 The committee discussed the importance of maintaining strong relationships with local
community groups, and agreed that the library’s role as a community hub is a key priority.
It was noted that the library’s meeting rooms are well utilised by community groups, with an
average of 15 bookings per month.

**8. Financial Report**

8.1 The Library Manager tabled the financial report for the period 1 September to 30 September
2018. The report was noted as being consistent with the budget, with no significant variances
identified.

8.2 *Expenditure* – Total expenditure for September was $182,400, which is 8.2% of the annual
budget. The main areas of expenditure were staff salaries ($121,000), collection development
($28,500), and programs and events ($12,900). The expenditure on collection development was
slightly higher than anticipated due to the purchase of new non-fiction titles, which was
approved at the previous meeting.

**10. Other Business**

10.1 The committee noted that the Library will be closed on the second Monday of
November for staff professional development. The closure is consistent with the
arrangement approved by Council, and notices have been placed on the Library
website and at the front desk. The Library will reopen at 9.30am the following day.

10.2 Councillor Nguyen raised the matter of the library’s volunteer program. He
asked whether the committee had received an update on the number of active
volunteers, as the figure had not been reported for some time. The Library
Manager advised that a full volunteer report has been scheduled for the February
2019 meeting, and that current volunteer numbers are stable. She confirmed that
the volunteer coordinator position remains vacant, and that recruitment for that
role is being handled by Council’s HR section. Councillor Nguyen asked that the
report include a breakdown of volunteer hours by activity, and the Library
Manager agreed to include this.

10.3 Cr Demetriou asked whether the library had given any further thought to
extending the opening hours on Wednesday evenings. The Library Manager advised
that the matter had been discussed with Council’s property section, and that a
costing had been prepared. The costing assumes an additional two hours per week,
with staffing provided by a combination of existing casual staff and a new
permanent part-time position. The Library Manager will circulate the costing to
committee members by email prior to the next meeting, and the matter will be
listed for discussion under other business at that time.

10.4 The committee discussed the proposal from the Marrickville Seniors Centre
regarding intergenerational reading sessions, which was raised earlier in the
meeting. It was agreed that Ms Moretti would bring a draft proposal to the next
meeting, and that the proposal should include an outline of the session format,
an indication of the number of children and seniors that could be accommodated,
and a plan for the recruitment of child participants through local primary
schools. The committee expressed general support for the concept, and noted that
the Library’s meeting room would be a suitable venue.

**11. Reports from Sub-Committees and Working Groups**

11.1 The Library Manager reported that the Local History Working Group had met
on 2 October 2018. The group has been focused on the digitisation of the
Marrickville area’s early council rate books, which are held in the local
history collection. The group has completed the scanning of the rate books for
the years 1890 to 1895, and is now in the process of checking the quality of the
scans and preparing the associated index. The index is being prepared by
volunteers, and the group expects the work to be completed by the end of the
year. A short article on the project will be included in the next edition of the
library’s newsletter.

11.2 The Library Manager reported that the Children’s and Youth Services Working
Group had met on 9 October 2018. The group discussed the summer school holiday
program, which is currently being planned. The program will run from mid-
December 2018 to the end of January 2019, and will include a mix of free and
low-cost activities. The group has confirmed that the popular “Lego Club” will
be offered on a weekly basis, and that a new robotics workshop will be
introduced, subject to the availability of a suitable facilitator. The Library
Manager will provide a more detailed program outline at the next meeting.

11.3 The committee noted the minutes of the two working groups, which had been
circulated with the agenda.

**12. Staff Matters**

12.1 The Library Manager reported that the temporary library assistant who had
been employed to cover maternity leave has had her contract extended for a
further three months. The extension is effective from 1 November 2018, and will
ensure continuity of staffing through the busy summer period.
